:::{#exm-differentiable-on}
#### Differentiable on one interval but not another

- $f(x) = x^2$ is differentiable on $[0, 1]$:
  the computation of @exm-differentiable with $3$ replaced by any $c$
  gives $\tfrac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h} = 2c + h$, which tends to $2c$,
  including the one-sided limits at the endpoints $0$ and $1$.
- $g(x) = \sqrt[3]{x}$ is differentiable on $[1, 2]$,
  but not on $[-1, 1]$: the point $0$ is in $[-1, 1]$ and is not an endpoint,
  and @exm-differentiable shows $g$ is not differentiable there.

:::
